# Review instructions

How Claude reviews a pull request in this repo (playbook Stage 5, "AI in the PR review loop"). Written by the tech lead (sample data:
Khoa). Findings are advisory: they never approve or block a pull request. A person approves.

Read first: the diff, `CLAUDE.md`, and the spec and plan the pull request names in `PR.md` (`spec/`, `plan/`). Read the policies in
`.claude/skills/policy-*/SKILL.md` when a change touches what they cover.

## Passes

Run three passes, in this order. Each finding belongs to exactly one pass.

1. **Bugs**: logic errors, wrong edge cases (empty list, filter active, one item, many items), state that is saved but not shown or shown
   but not saved, broken keyboard use.
2. **Security**: `policy-security`. User text reaches the page only through `textContent` (S3). Imported files are validated (S1). No new
   network request, script, CDN or dependency (S4). Nothing destructive without a confirm (S2).
3. **Compliance**: the change does what its accepted spec and plan say, and nothing the spec puts out of scope. UI text follows
   `policy-ux` (Vietnamese, short, no technical words). `CLAUDE.md` rules (size of change, tests with the fix).

## What Important means here

A finding is **Important** if it would break behaviour a user relies on, lose or leak data, or breach a policy or an accepted spec.
Everything else is a **Nit**: naming, formatting, comments, style, a cleaner way to write the same thing.

If you are not sure a problem is real, say what you would check, and mark it Nit.

## Cap the nits

At most **5 nits** per review. Pick the ones most worth a person's time. Say how many you dropped.

## Do not report

- Anything `bash scripts/check.sh` already checks (tests pass, syntax).
- `demo/`, `evals/results/`, `review/`: evidence and generated output.
- Wording inside `tickets/` and `docs/`: not working files.
- Praise, summaries of what the diff does, or restating the PR description.

## Also say

- If the change makes `CLAUDE.md` out of date (a command, a rule, a file it names), report it as a Compliance finding.
- If the same mistake is already listed under "Things Claude gets wrong" in `CLAUDE.md`, say so: the line is not working.

9	
10	Sample standard for the demo. Each rule has an ID; cite it as `policy-ux@2#U<n>`.
11	
12	- **U1.** Never lose the user's data silently. Any failed save is shown on the same screen, in plain words, with what the user can do
13	  next.
14	- **U2.** No confirmation dialogs for actions on a single item: they happen at once and offer **Undo** for 10 seconds instead.
15	  Actions that overwrite or delete more than one item follow `policy-security#S2` (confirm first). *(Changed in v2, agreed by the UX
16	  and security owners, 2026-10-20.)*
17	- **U3.** Every list or screen defines its empty, loading and error states.
18	- **U4.** UI text is Vietnamese, short, and free of technical words (no "localStorage", "JSON", "console").
19	- **U5.** Every control works with the keyboard and has an accessible label.

---
name: policy-ux
description: UX standard of the todo app team (version 2). Rules for feedback on failures, confirmations, screen states, wording and accessibility. Load it whenever you write or review a spec, design or UI code for the app.
version: 2
owner: Linh (UX owner, simulated) · backup: Thảo (product owner, simulated)
---

# UX standard · v2

Sample standard for the demo. Each rule has an ID; cite it as `policy-ux@2#U<n>`.

- **U1.** Never lose the user's data silently. Any failed save is shown on the same screen, in plain words, with what the user can do
  next.
- **U2.** No confirmation dialogs for actions on a single item: they happen at once and offer **Undo** for 10 seconds instead.
  Actions that overwrite or delete more than one item follow `policy-security#S2` (confirm first). *(Changed in v2, agreed by the UX
  and security owners, 2026-10-20.)*
- **U3.** Every list or screen defines its empty, loading and error states.
- **U4.** UI text is Vietnamese, short, and free of technical words (no "localStorage", "JSON", "console").
- **U5.** Every control works with the keyboard and has an accessible label.

1	---
2	name: policy-security
3	description: Security policy of the todo app team (version 1). Rules for input handling, destructive operations, rendering user text and dependencies. Load it whenever you write or review a spec, design or code that reads files or input, deletes or overwrites data, renders user text, or adds a dependency.
4	version: 1
5	owner: Khoa (tech lead, also security owner, simulated) · backup: Mai (simulated)
6	---
7	
8	# Security policy · v1
9	
10	Sample policy for the demo. Each rule has an ID; cite it as `policy-security@1#S<n>`.
11	
12	- **S1.** Treat every imported file as untrusted. Validate it against the expected schema, reject unknown fields, cap its size at
13	  1 MB, never evaluate its content.
14	- **S2.** Any operation that overwrites or deletes more than one item asks for an explicit confirmation **before** it runs, and the
15	  confirmation says what will be lost (for example "Thay 12 việc hiện có bằng 30 việc trong file?").
16	- **S3.** Render user-provided text with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.
17	- **S4.** No new external dependency (CDN script, library, web service) without sign-off from the security owner.
18

file.content:
---
name: policy-security
description: Security policy of the todo app team (version 1). Rules for input handling, destructive operations, rendering user text and dependencies. Load it whenever you write or review a spec, design or code that reads files or input, deletes or overwrites data, renders user text, or adds a dependency.
version: 1
owner: Khoa (tech lead, also security owner, simulated) · backup: Mai (simulated)
---

# Security policy · v1

Sample policy for the demo. Each rule has an ID; cite it as `policy-security@1#S<n>`.

- **S1.** Treat every imported file as untrusted. Validate it against the expected schema, reject unknown fields, cap its size at
  1 MB, never evaluate its content.
- **S2.** Any operation that overwrites or deletes more than one item asks for an explicit confirmation **before** it runs, and the
  confirmation says what will be lost (for example "Thay 12 việc hiện có bằng 30 việc trong file?").
- **S3.** Render user-provided text with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.
- **S4.** No new external dependency (CDN script, library, web service) without sign-off from the security owner.
